source.title: Stochastic Weighted Function Norm Regularization
source.authors: A. Triki; Maxim Berman; Matthew B. Blaschko

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and supplementary material. Its title in the text is “Function Norms and Regularization in Deep Neural Networks,” differing from the supplied title metadata.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares dropout with no-dropout settings and reports held-out classification performance, directly testing dropout’s effect in its MNIST setting.
record.gate_note: The study also compares weighted function-norm regularization with dropout and batch normalization. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out MNIST accuracy with and without dropout in LeNet trained on very small subsets, including combinations with function-norm regularization. These results bear on V6 in a new regularization setting, although the supplied figure text does not resolve every comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report improved performance from weighted function-norm regularization over the tested conventional regularizers, an apparent further gain when combined with dropout, and apparent suppression of the function-norm benefit by batch normalization. They do not explicitly conclude that dropout alone improves accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Tests dropout in a low-data MNIST regularization comparison using LeNet; it is not presented as a reproduction of the dropout study.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different outcomes by regularization batch size and says batch normalization seems to annihilate the function-norm effect. Gaussian sampling with mean 5 and variance 2, or mean 10 and variance 1, caused training to diverge; these are function-norm sampling conditions, not dropout results.

fits_no_version.finding: Weighted function-norm regularization improves classification and segmentation performance relative to the tested baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling-based weighted function-norm penalties can improve held-out performance in low-data classification and segmentation.

record.problems: Dropout comparisons are presented as curves without numerical values in the supplied text. The authors do not explicitly state that dropout itself improves held-out accuracy in the tested comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-linked rows were extractable: dropout-related plotted comparisons are captured in R1 and R2, and their values are figure-only.

untested.parts: No original random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization experiment.
No network-width sweep or test of generalization beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or manipulation of local connectivity.
No controlled comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
No training-batch comparison under a fixed epoch budget. Changing the function-norm estimation batch does not test this version.

No readable conclusion for dropout alone; no dropout-strength sweep demonstrating underfitting; no joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation. Larger-data regimes and fully connected classifier results are not tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, gap-ranking comparison, or perturbation experiment.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

missing.what: Figure 3a contains additional dropout-only and combined dropout/function-norm comparisons under Gaussian sampling, with and without weight decay. R1 and R2 cover only VAE sampling in Figure 2a. The additional conditions need rows, even if their dropout effects remain unreadable.

Figure 8 presents corresponding regularization conditions without and with dropout using 300 MNIST training examples. These comparisons are omitted from the record. The supplied text does not establish their numerical dropout effects or whether the panels share training subsets, so those details require verification before assigning a verdict.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. Figure curves are not reconstructable from the supplied text; axis labels alone do not establish dropout effects. R2's qualitative result supports a narrowly conditional verdict, without establishing effect size or significance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are discussed through cited work, not tested here.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
The study uses SGD with momentum for its main MNIST model and Adam for the VAE, but does not compare optimizer generalization.

Dropout comparisons are shown in figures without recoverable numeric values or a clear text statement that dropout itself lowers held-out error. The study does not test dropout on very small training sets as a failure condition or the joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.

rows.note: The authors state that combining their regularizer with dropout seems to increase performance, but the figure does not provide recoverable numerical values; this does not isolate dropout’s effect against a no-dropout baseline.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report an apparent further performance improvement when dropout is combined with function-norm regularization. This supports the incremental dropout comparison against function-norm regularization alone; the record incorrectly says that comparison cannot isolate dropout's effect. Magnitude and statistical significance remain unavailable.
